reader.requirement: At --std 85, when an FD carries a CODE-SET clause, every signed numeric elementary data description entry associated with that FD must be described with SIGN ... SEPARATE CHARACTER, either by its own SIGN clause or by a group SIGN clause that applies to it (GR1-GR3 precedence, an elementary item's own non-separate clause overriding a group's SEPARATE one); a signed item with no SIGN clause or a non-separate one must be refused, and signed items outside such an FD are unaffected.

edition-consulted.switches: binder.Edition.DialectLevel < 2002 adds CheckCodeSetReportItems (a report file's printable items screened by the same predicate, §1985:VII.3.4.3 SR1); the record-item arm is the same code at every edition

ChoiceIndicators.AlphabetPair / the version gate refuse the 2002 'FOR ALPHANUMERIC/NATIONAL' phrases at --std 85 (COBOL0900); the class the clause selects (CodeSetRecordClass) is the same at every edition

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for record description entries; at 85 the same screen also covers a report file's printable items (an extra 1985 arm, which refused a non-separate signed report item in probe s11)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness covers a group-inherited SIGN LEADING SEPARATE that must compile; the refusal half (no SIGN clause, non-separate SIGN, an elementary non-separate clause overriding a group's SEPARATE) is not exercised by it

probes.expected: report file data under CODE-SET screened alike at 85

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.5.12.3 SR3  (5.12.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR3

reader.notes: The screen runs after InheritSignClauses, so it reads each elementary item's effective sign kind; any signed DISPLAY item whose kind is not separate is refused at the item. A first probe spelled `SIGN SEPARATE` without LEADING/TRAILING and was refused COBOL5506, which is correct: §1985:VI.5.12.2 requires LEADING or TRAILING.
